profile: Stock PostgreSQL 16.6 and 17.2, UTF-8, standard-conforming strings and native parameters. A named application schema is a persistent local namespace.
scope: Stand-alone REINDEX SCHEMA with the ordered concurrency flags and known selected application namespace. The native selection includes ordinary table and materialized-view indexes and their auxiliary TOAST indexes. In a partitioned layout the selected schema fixes each leaf's eligibility.

Schema/Index/ReindexSchema.role: A complete rebuild that selects an explicitly identified persistent application schema.
Schema/Index/ReindexSchema.structure: One decoded schema identifier, the effective native rebuild-mode enum and one grammar release.
Schema/Index/ReindexSchema.conditions: The direct value admits application namespace identifiers in the selected profile. System scopes and temporary aliases have separate native rules. The analyzer requires a known persistent schema, rejects unsupported options and chooses the final concurrency request.
Schema/Index/ReindexSchema.meaning: Rebuild the eligible indexes physically owned by relations in the selected namespace. Owners elsewhere, including attached descendants in a different schema, remain unchanged. A schema rebuild is prohibited inside an active transaction in both modes.
Schema/Index/ReindexSchema.sql: Emit REINDEX SCHEMA followed by the effective optional CONCURRENTLY keyword and one quoted schema identifier.
Schema/Index/ReindexSchema.externalInterpretation: Use the same application namespace and relation catalog, eligible physical index definitions, release, modes and transaction state.

rules: An empty eligible index set succeeds outside a transaction.
A standard rebuild changes each eligible storage file while retaining the index OID. A concurrent rebuild can replace the OID and physical file together.
Schema selection follows each physical owner's namespace. A partitioned parent in that namespace can have children in other namespaces. Auxiliary indexes follow their selected owner.
Native execution requires a top-level command even in standard mode. A transaction failure leaves both the selected namespace and the decoy unchanged.
The stock engine resolves a schema selector literally. The session alias pg_temp is not an application namespace for this operation.
observations: Exact bound schema and mode, rendering, status, transaction state and notices.
The physical heap and index identity relations, named index attachment roles, selected and decoy typed rows, and native catalog layout across phases.

finite.identity: Consume all 32 coordinates through both direct construction and already bound SQL on each native release. Reconcile the observed schema, mode and the full native selection.

exploration.domain: Vary retained name quoting and dotted identifiers, ordered concurrency options, empty and populated effect sets, transaction state, visible and auxiliary indexes, partition ownership and distinct decoy data.

negative: Unknown schema in an open declaration set
faults: Reduce the scope to one owner
Drop the effective concurrent mode and its index identity transition
trust: Checked typed constructor and renderer, supplied catalog consistency, verified native physical identity observations, and immutable external replay schedule.
open: Database and system-wide selectors, temporary numbered namespace references, tablespace, verbosity and invalid or exclusion-index observations remain distinct obligations.
